title: CFTC Sends Crypto Market-Structure Rule to White House Review
description: Two days after the CLARITY Act stalled, the CFTC submitted a proposed rulemaking titled 'Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets' to the White House Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs. Chairman Michael Selig has said the rule would let registered and currently unregistered crypto exchanges be designated as a new type of designated contract market offering leveraged or margined crypto trading under CFTC oversight. A public proposal is expected once the review, typically up to 60 days, is complete.

title: House Panels Advance Bitcoin Reserve and Crypto Tax Bills
description: A day after the CLARITY Act failed in the Senate, the House Financial Services Committee advanced H.R. 8957, the American Reserve Modernization Act, 28-21 on party lines. It would write the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve into statute, bar sales, swaps or encumbrances for a minimum of 20 years and give Treasury 180 days to stand up the reserve and a separate Digital Asset Stockpile, without mandating purchases. The same day the Ways and Means Committee advanced H.R. 10357, the Digital Asset Tax Certainty Act, 38-5, extending wash-sale rules to widely traded digital assets, exempting network fees of $10 or less and setting rules for mining, staking, stablecoins and crypto lending. Both bills await House floor votes and have no Senate companion.

title: CLARITY Act Fails Senate Cloture Vote
description: The Senate failed to invoke cloture on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (H.R. 3633), with the motion drawing 50 votes against the 60 required. Democrats who had negotiated the text voted no over ethics provisions on officials’ crypto holdings that they said did not effectively reach the president and his family. The vote, set up when Majority Leader Thune filed cloture on 8 August, effectively ends market-structure legislation for 2026 and shifts the action to SEC and CFTC rulemaking; bitcoin fell about 4% on the day.

title: Polish Sejm Fails to Override Third Veto of Crypto-Asset Act
description: The Sejm voted 241-198 with three abstentions to override President Nawrocki’s veto of the Crypto-Asset Market Act, 25 votes short of the three-fifths threshold of 266. It was the third vetoed version since December 2025; the president argues the rules are excessively burdensome and would push firms to other EU jurisdictions. The bill would have made the KNF Poland’s MiCA supervisor, so Poland remains the only EU member without a domestic licensing path and local firms must seek authorisation elsewhere in the bloc while passported foreign providers can still serve Polish clients.

title: IMF Review Confirms El Salvador BTC Additions Came From Donations
description: IMF staff reached agreement with El Salvador on the combined second and third reviews of its roughly $1.4 billion Extended Fund Facility, unlocking about $140 million subject to Board approval. The IMF confirmed that no public funds have been used to buy bitcoin since mid-2025 and that additions to the national reserve, now about 7,764 BTC, came from private donations. Majority ownership of the state Chivo wallet has been transferred to a private operator, and bitcoin keeps its legal-tender status under the 2025 amendments that made acceptance voluntary.

title: Pakistan Opens Crypto Licensing Under the Virtual Assets Act
description: The Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority notified its final regulations under the Virtual Assets Act 2026 and opened a licensing portal with ten licence categories spanning exchange, custody, broker-dealer, advisory, lending, derivatives, asset management, transfer and settlement, issuance and mining-related services. Existing providers had until 5 September 2026 to apply for a no-objection certificate or cease operations. Chairman Bilal bin Saqib described the framework as a legal front door for domestic and global firms into a market that had operated outside the law.

title: SEC Proposes Regulation Crypto Assets, First Bespoke Offering Regime
description: The SEC proposed Regulation Crypto Assets, its first permanent rule tailored to digital assets. It creates two offering exemptions, up to $5 million over four years and up to $75 million per 12-month period with financial statements and ongoing reporting, both with principles-based disclosure and preemption of state registration. It also adds a conditional safe harbor under which a crypto asset is no longer treated as an investment contract once the issuer’s essential managerial efforts are complete. The proposal has a 60-day comment period from Federal Register publication.

title: Hong Kong’s First Licensed HKD Stablecoin Goes Live
description: Anchorpoint Financial, the Standard Chartered, HKT and Animoca Brands joint venture, began a phase-one rollout of HKDAP (Hong Kong dollar at par) to institutional and professional investors through HashKey Exchange and OSL, the first stablecoin issued under the Stablecoins Ordinance. Anchorpoint and HSBC received the HKMA’s first two issuer licences in April 2026. Retail access is targeted for late 2026, and HSBC plans its own HKD stablecoin in the second half of 2026.

title: Putin Signs Law Legalising Regulated Crypto Trading
description: President Putin signed Russia’s first comprehensive crypto market law in early August, bringing exchanges, custodians, brokers and clearing houses under Bank of Russia supervision from 1 September 2026, with issuance and circulation rules following on 1 September 2027. Exchanges must join a central bank registry, hold at least 15 million rubles (about $185,000) in capital and join a self-regulatory body; non-qualified retail investors must pass a suitability test and are capped at 300,000 rubles (about $3,700) a year per intermediary. Domestic crypto payments remain banned, while cross-border settlement of foreign-trade contracts is permitted.

title: Kenya Gazettes VASP Regulations, Activating Licensing Regime
description: The National Treasury gazetted the Virtual Asset Service Providers Regulations 2026 (Legal Notice No. 134), operationalising the VASP Act that President Ruto signed in October 2025. The Central Bank of Kenya licenses fiat-conversion services and stablecoin issuers, while the Capital Markets Authority licenses exchanges, token issuance, ICOs and tokenisation, and the central bank may restrict access to offshore stablecoins. Existing operators must be licensed by 4 November 2026, one year after the Act commenced.

title: Japan Moves Crypto Under Securities Law, Opening ETF Path
description: The Diet gave final approval to amendments to the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act that reclassify crypto assets as financial instruments from fiscal 2027, adding insider-trading and disclosure rules and raising penalties for unregistered operators to 10 years’ prison and ¥10 million. The change removes the main legal hurdle to spot bitcoin ETFs in Japan. Under the linked tax reform, gains on crypto traded through licensed exchanges move to a flat 20% separate tax from 2028, down from progressive rates of up to 55%.

title: Kazakhstan Grants 3-Year Crypto Tax Exemption via Licensed Platforms
description: President Tokayev signed a decree exempting individuals’ digital-asset income from personal income tax for three years when earned through Kazakhstan’s licensed domestic platforms, paired with a voluntary disclosure window for holders who move assets from foreign or unregulated venues to licensed providers by the end of 2026. The package also allows associated gas from oil fields to power mining and promotes digital assets and stablecoins for cross-border settlement, building on the digital financial assets law that took effect on 1 May 2026.

title: MiCA Transitional Period Ends; Unlicensed CASPs Must Exit EU
description: The grandfathering period under the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation expired on 1 July 2026, making MiCA authorisation mandatory for any crypto-asset service provider serving EU and EEA clients. ESMA told unauthorised firms to stop providing services and execute orderly wind-down plans, migrating client assets to authorised providers or self-custody. Around 244 CASPs were authorised at the deadline, including Coinbase, Kraken and Bitstamp.

title: Taiwan Passes Virtual Asset Service Act With Full Licensing Regime
description: The Legislative Yuan passed Taiwan’s first dedicated crypto statute on its third reading, replacing the AML-registration regime with FSC licensing for all virtual asset service providers. Stablecoin issuers need approval from both the central bank and the FSC and must hold full reserves; unlicensed operation carries up to seven years’ prison and a NT$100 million fine. Firms already registered for AML get 12 months to apply and up to 21 months to be licensed, with the Executive Yuan to set the effective date.

title: FCA Publishes Final Rules for UK Cryptoasset Regime
description: The FCA published the final policy statements completing its crypto roadmap, covering trading platforms, intermediaries, custody, qualifying stablecoin issuance, staking, prudential requirements and a crypto market-abuse regime. The authorisation gateway opens on 30 September 2026, applications close on 28 February 2027 and the regime goes live on 25 October 2027. The Bank of England separately published its policy statement for systemic sterling stablecoins on 22 June.

title: Senate Banking Committee Advances CLARITY Act
description: The Senate Banking Committee advanced the Digital Asset Market Clarity (CLARITY) Act by a 15-9 vote, with all 13 Republicans joined by two Democrats. The market-structure bill would grant the CFTC exclusive jurisdiction over digital commodity spot markets while the SEC retains investment-contract assets. Outstanding issues include an ethics provision on officials' crypto ties before a floor vote.

title: US Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Custody Framework Formalised
description: In March 2026 the US formalised the custody and governance framework behind the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve, with publicly reported government holdings around 325,000–328,000 BTC. The framework codifies long-term hold policy for seized and acquired coins, while the BITCOIN Act — mandating purchase of up to 1 million BTC over five years with a 20-year minimum hold — remains pending in Congress.

title: Brazil Reintroduces RESBit National Bitcoin Reserve Bill
description: Brazil's Congress reintroduced legislation proposing a sovereign Bitcoin reserve (RESBit) that would accumulate up to 1 million BTC over five years — roughly 5% of total supply — managed by the Central Bank and Finance Ministry. The bill positions Brazil as the largest emerging market pursuing strategic Bitcoin accumulation.

title: Hong Kong Stablecoins Ordinance Takes Effect
description: Hong Kong's Stablecoins Ordinance came into force, requiring HKMA licences for issuers of fiat-referenced stablecoins issued in Hong Kong or referencing the HK dollar. The regime — full reserve backing, redemption at par, and ongoing disclosure — anchors Hong Kong's bid to be Asia's regulated digital-asset hub.

title: GENIUS Act Signed — US Stablecoin Framework
description: President Trump signed the GENIUS Act, the first comprehensive US federal framework for payment stablecoins. Issuers must back tokens 1:1 with cash or short-term Treasuries and publish monthly reserve disclosures. The law was widely read as the first leg of full US digital-asset regulatory clarity.

title: CLARITY Act Passes US House 294-134
description: The House passed the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act with a strong bipartisan majority, establishing the first comprehensive US market-structure framework for digital assets and splitting oversight between the CFTC (digital commodities) and SEC (investment contracts).

title: Pakistan Announces Strategic Bitcoin Reserve
description: Pakistan announced a government-led Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and allocated surplus power capacity for Bitcoin mining, a sharp pivot from years of central-bank restrictions. The newly formed Pakistan Crypto Council is driving licensing and a national digital-asset framework.

title: SEC Dismisses Coinbase Enforcement Action
description: The SEC dismissed its civil enforcement action against Coinbase with prejudice, reversing the agency's enforcement-led approach to crypto. With the new Crypto Task Force chartered to build a clear framework, the SEC subsequently wound down most major crypto enforcement cases, including Ripple.

title: El Salvador Makes Bitcoin Acceptance Voluntary (IMF Deal)
description: El Salvador's Congress amended the Bitcoin Law 55-2, making private-sector acceptance of BTC voluntary and ending its use for tax payments, as required by a $1.4B IMF loan agreement. Bitcoin keeps nominal legal-tender designation but is no longer defined as 'currency'. The government continues accumulating BTC for its national reserve despite the rollback.

title: US Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Established
description: President Trump signed an executive order establishing a US Strategic Bitcoin Reserve, directing the Treasury to hold and not sell Bitcoin seized by the federal government. A separate digital asset stockpile was also created for other seized cryptocurrencies.

title: Trump Signs Pro-Crypto Executive Order
description: President Trump signed an executive order directing federal agencies to promote digital asset development, protect the right to self-custody, and establish a Presidential Working Group on Digital Asset Markets. The order also rescinded prior restrictive crypto policy guidance.

title: Hong Kong Approves Spot Bitcoin & Ether ETFs
description: Hong Kong's SFC approved spot Bitcoin and Ether ETF listings for three issuers — ChinaAMC, Bosera, and HashKey. The move positions Hong Kong as the first major Asian financial hub to allow retail access to spot crypto ETFs.

title: SEC Approves 11 Spot Bitcoin ETFs
description: After a decade of rejections, the SEC approved spot Bitcoin ETF applications from BlackRock iShares, Fidelity, Ark 21Shares, Invesco, and seven others. Combined first-day trading volume exceeded $4.6 billion, making it one of the most successful ETF launches in history.

title: Grayscale Wins vs SEC in DC Circuit Court
description: The US Court of Appeals for the DC Circuit ruled in favour of Grayscale, finding the SEC's rejection of GBTC's conversion to a spot ETF was 'arbitrary and capricious.' The ruling was widely seen as a catalyst for the eventual spot ETF approvals in January 2024.

title: EU MiCA Regulation Enacted
description: The EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation was published in the Official Journal, creating the world's first comprehensive crypto regulatory framework for a major economic bloc. MiCA covers issuers of crypto-assets and CASPs, with full application from December 2024.

title: SEC Sues Coinbase and Binance
description: The SEC filed lawsuits against Coinbase (for operating as an unregistered securities exchange) and Binance (for broader securities violations including commingling funds). The dual enforcement actions intensified regulatory uncertainty for the entire crypto industry.

title: Ripple Partial Win vs SEC
description: Judge Analisa Torres ruled that XRP sold on secondary market exchanges did not constitute securities, handing Ripple a partial victory against the SEC. While institutional sales were found to be securities, the ruling offered a framework distinction that benefited the broader crypto market.

title: UAE Exempts Crypto from Capital Gains Tax
description: The UAE Federal Tax Authority confirmed that virtual assets and related transactions, including transfers and conversions, are exempt from VAT, with zero capital gains tax on crypto. The policy reinforces the UAE's position as a global crypto hub.

title: Australia Advances Crypto Exchange Licensing
description: ASIC issued updated guidance clarifying that crypto exchanges holding customer assets require an Australian Financial Services (AFS) licence. The framework aligns crypto custody with traditional financial services regulation.

title: Switzerland DLT Act Fully Operative
description: Switzerland's DLT Act — amending nine federal laws to accommodate distributed ledger technology — came into full effect, providing legal clarity for tokenised securities, DeFi, and digital asset custodians. Switzerland continues to lead Europe in crypto-friendly legislation.

title: Brazil Crypto Legal Framework Enacted
description: Brazil's Virtual Asset Service Provider Act (Law 14,478) took effect, establishing a licensing regime for crypto exchanges and a legal definition of virtual assets. The Central Bank of Brazil was designated as the primary regulator.

title: MAS Issues Stablecoin Regulatory Framework
description: The Monetary Authority of Singapore published its final stablecoin framework, requiring single-currency stablecoins pegged to SGD or G10 currencies to maintain full reserve backing and meet capital requirements. Non-compliant stablecoins may not call themselves MAS-regulated.

title: US Executive Order on Digital Assets
description: President Biden signed EO 14067 directing federal agencies to produce coordinated reports on crypto risks, benefits, and regulatory approaches. The order was broadly considered a signal that the US was moving toward a comprehensive crypto framework rather than an outright ban.

title: India Introduces 30% Crypto Tax
description: India's Finance Act introduced a 30% flat tax on income from virtual digital assets and a 1% TDS on transfers. The punitive tax structure — with no ability to offset losses across assets — was widely seen as discouraging domestic crypto activity.

title: CAR Adopts Bitcoin as Legal Tender
description: The Central African Republic became the second country in the world to adopt Bitcoin as legal tender, passing the bill unanimously in parliament. The move was described as a step toward economic sovereignty, though practical adoption remains limited by low internet penetration.

title: Germany Confirms Bitcoin Tax-Free After 1 Year
description: Germany's Federal Ministry of Finance formally confirmed that Bitcoin and Ether held for more than one year are exempt from capital gains tax for retail investors — regardless of whether coins were used in staking or lending. Germany remains the most favourable G7 country for long-term Bitcoin holders.

title: Canada Launches World's First Bitcoin ETF
description: Purpose Bitcoin ETF (BTCC) launched on the Toronto Stock Exchange, becoming the world's first exchange-listed spot Bitcoin ETF. It attracted over $400 million in assets in its first two days of trading.

title: El Salvador Makes Bitcoin Legal Tender
description: El Salvador became the first country in history to adopt Bitcoin as legal tender under the Bitcoin Law passed by the Legislative Assembly. The government launched the Chivo wallet and distributed $30 in BTC to citizens. The IMF expressed concerns over financial stability risks.

title: China Bans Bitcoin Mining
description: China's State Council Financial Stability and Development Committee called for a crackdown on Bitcoin mining and trading. Provincial governments including Inner Mongolia, Sichuan, and Xinjiang followed with immediate shutdowns, relocating roughly 50-60% of global hash rate abroad.

title: China Declares All Crypto Transactions Illegal
description: Ten Chinese agencies including the PBOC, NDRC, and MPS jointly declared all cryptocurrency transactions illegal and banned foreign exchanges from serving Chinese users. The blanket ban extended to DeFi and NFTs, making China's prohibition among the most comprehensive globally.

title: US Infrastructure Bill Expands Crypto Tax Reporting
description: The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act broadened the definition of 'broker' to include crypto custodians, exchanges, and potentially miners and validators. The expanded reporting requirements obligate brokers to issue 1099s for crypto transactions, raising compliance costs significantly.

title: Turkey Bans Crypto Payments
description: Turkey's central bank (CBRT) banned the use of cryptocurrencies and crypto-backed instruments as a means of payment for goods and services. The ban was attributed to risks including price volatility and potential use in illicit activity. Crypto trading on exchanges remained permitted.

title: SEC Rejects Bitwise and VanEck Spot ETF Filings
description: The SEC rejected multiple spot Bitcoin ETF proposals including those from Bitwise and VanEck, citing concerns about market manipulation and the lack of surveillance-sharing agreements with regulated Bitcoin markets. The rejections set off a multi-year campaign by asset managers to meet SEC standards.

title: Japan Recognises Bitcoin as Legal Property
description: Japan's Payment Services Act amendments came into effect, recognising Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies as legal property and creating one of the world's first formal crypto exchange licensing regimes under the FSA. The framework became a model for balanced crypto regulation globally.
